issue_context.title: HPA should consider individual containers when scaling based on resource metrics
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
Currently when calculating the utilization of resources on pods the usage of all the containers in the pods is summed and then divided by the sum of the requested resources of all containers. The HPA should have a way of specifying how the utilization should be computed. If it should be the sum of the containers, or if it should be the average of the individual container utilization or the maximum of the utilization of the containers. 

**Why is this needed**:
Consider the case when there are multiple containers in the pods, with one main container and a few sidecar containers which are over provisioned. If the main container consumes a lot of resources and is close to its requests the HPA would consider the utilization of the pod to be within limits. This would prevent scaling out. The inverse could also be true. Sidecars are sometimes necessary for the main container to function correctly. If one of the sidecars slowly down with high utilization the HPA would not scale out the target because the average utilization of the pod is still low.

review_comments: is there a reason not to use the same schema as v2beta2 ContainerResourceMetricSource here? that would simplify (and maybe eliminate the need for) custom conversion methods. same question applies to v1 ContainerResourceMetricSource and the v1/v2beta1 ContainerResourceMetricStatus types

It looks like the schema in v2beta2 uses MetricTarget which only exists in v2beta2. Would it be worth copying that to v1/v2beta1 for use here? I don't have a strong opinion whether it's better to keep the v1/v2beta1 bit consistent with existing v1/v2beta1 metric specs, or to keep this new field consistent across versions.
v2beta2 metric target was expanded and unified averageUtilization/averageValue... that doesn't exist in v1 or v2beta1
cc @kubernetes/sig-cli-pr-reviews
Added validation
think about what bounds we place on all new fields. e.g. should this be length-constrained? limited to specific characters?
I have changed it to use an existing helper method which validates that the resource is a valid container resource.
document the meaning of `container==""` in the interface godoc here
Added explanation.

As mentioned above (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90691#discussion_r463440392):

If a container is missing entirely, this will return a resource request of zero.  This is not ideal.  If the targeted container is missing, we should treat it as an invalid configuration and return an error.
@josephburnett I've updated the logic to return an error in case the pod metrics endpoint does not return metrics about the the container.

add `ContainerResource` to the list of valid types in the docs for the `type` field, noting `ContainerResource` is alpha-level and requires the HPAContainerMetrics feature to be enabled (comment applies to types.go for all API versions)
cc @kubernetes/sig-cli-pr-reviews
defer to @kubernetes/sig-autoscaling-pr-reviews on controller review
@kubernetes/sig-autoscaling-pr-reviews
the same feature-gate would protect this field

Both during the create and the update checks the status cannot be set. During create it is set to [empty](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/14a11060a0775ed609f0810898ebdbe737c59441/pkg/registry/autoscaling/horizontalpodautoscaler/strategy.go#L50). And during an update it would not be [allowed to update to the new value](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/14a11060a0775ed609f0810898ebdbe737c59441/pkg/registry/autoscaling/horizontalpodautoscaler/strategy.go#L73). So the resource status does not have to be explicitly set to an empty object IMO. For the metric source I have added filtering so that when the feature gate is not enabled the new metric source type is filtered out.
in autoscalerStatusStrategy#PrepareForUpdate, follow the pattern of clearing the field if the feature is off AND the existing object does not use the new field

Updating the status is not allowed in the strategy. So for cases when the feature gate if off it will simply get copied over from the old status if it exists. And it can only exist if the controller puts it there because the feature was enabled and used.
document this is only supported on servers that enable the alpha HPAContainerMetrics feature (note this in all the types.go files in the API doc for this field)
Added to the docs
not sure why this changed... see if this goes back to a pointer cast after removing the `PodResource *PodResourceMetricSource`
After removing the `PodMetricSource`this change was reverted. Looks like the tooling does not like aliased types.
